subject: Clarifying Redwood default log retention, residency, and delete options
messages:
From: Alex Reynolds <alex@acme-corp.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Quick Q: default retention for requests/outputs and residency

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited about Redwood's latency and cost numbers. Before we move to a POC, the security/compliance team asked for a few clarifications around default log retention and residency for request/response data (prompts + model outputs). High level questions:

- By default, how long does Redwood keep request & response logs for hosted API customers? Does that include raw prompts and outputs or just metadata?
- For EU customers, where are those logs stored by default? Is it single-region, multi-region, or configurable?
- If we request deletion of an account's logs, what is the typical SLA (pushed vs background purge)? Are there any retained audit copies?

We'd like concise answers we can share with our InfoSec. Happy to jump on a quick call if needed.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Reynolds
Head of Platform, Acme Corp
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reynolds <alex@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@acme-corp.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Quick Q: default retention for requests/outputs and residency

Alex —

Great questions, thanks for sending. Summary up top, followed by specifics and links to the attached matrix.

TL;DR: For Redwood Hosted (standard tier) the default request/response retention window is 30 days and includes full request payloads and model outputs (unless you enable input redaction or use a Private/Dedicated deployment where retention is configurable). EU-region hosted customers have their logs stored in EU regions by default (single primary region with cross-region backups for HA — backups are encrypted and have a shorter retention). Deletion requests are processed as background purge jobs; primary data deletion SLA is 72 hours for standard accounts, but audit logs (access/audit trail) are retained for 365 days by default for security reasons unless contractually negotiated.

More detail:
- Default retention: 30 days for hosted API request/response logs (this includes the prompt text, metadata, and model outputs). This default balances product debugging/quality monitoring with privacy. The 30-day window is the default for token-level logs and chat histories stored in our logging pipeline.
- Metadata vs payload: we store both metadata (timestamps, model, route, latency, token counts) and payloads (raw prompt + model output) unless the customer opts into our input-redaction feature or uses Private/Dedicated where they can disable payload retention.
- EU residency: for accounts created with EU residency the primary storage is in eu-central-1 (or equivalent region) — we route and persist logs to the chosen primary region only. For HA we maintain encrypted, short-lived cross-region snapshots (48–72 hour ttl) used for failover; these are not searchable in the console and are purged automatically.
- Deletion requests: customers can use the Delete Data API (link in matrix) to request a purge for an account's logs. For hosted standard accounts we start a background purge and typically complete removal from live indices within 72 hours; underlying object-store garbage collection may take up to 14 days to finalize in some edge cases. We provide a deletion confirmation webhook when purge completes.
- Audit traces: access/audit logs (who queried what, key usage, admin actions) are retained 365 days by default for compliance/forensics. These do not contain full prompt+output payloads but may reference object ids and timestamps. Extended retention for audit logs can be contracted.

Attached is a short matrix that highlights differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private offerings. Marissa, can you confirm the exact phrasing we use in the public docs for the 72-hour purge vs final object GC? Neha — any regulatory caveats I should flag for EU data subject requests (DSR) here?

Next steps: if Acme wants a shorter default retention we can scope a Dedicated or Private setup, or enable an enterprise opt-in on Hosted to set a custom retention (POC/contract required).

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick Q: default retention for requests/outputs and residency

Alex — quick follow up from a security/compliance perspective. A couple of clarifications to add to Rishi's note:

- DSRs & deletions: For EU customers, we support Data Subject Requests under GDPR. Deletion requests initiated by a data subject are scoped to the customer's account boundary (we don't service-delete global backups unless explicitly requested and contracted). For DSR workflows we provide an audit trail of actions taken.
- Backups & cold storage: Cross-region snapshots used for failover are short-lived by default (48–72 hours). We do not keep long-term cold backups of request payloads for hosted customers. If a customer requires longer cold retention for their own purposes, that must be explicitly enabled and scoped in the contract.
- Redaction: Recommend enabling our input-redaction pipeline for any PII-heavy use cases; that prevents writing sensitive fields to our token logs. Redaction is best-effort pre-ingestion — customers should also redact client-side for maximum assurance.
- SOC 2 evidence: Attached is a short doc describing where retention-related evidence lives and the process for getting extracts (we supply time-bounded extracts and attestations for audits).

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our compliance team to walk through Acme's requirements and confirm contractual language.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
